page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the Dplsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-accelerated AES cryptography, though it lacks AVX, AMX, and hyper-threading capabilities. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance and memory efficiency. The D32pls_v6 achieves top-tier results in uncached large-block memory bandwidth, with read speeds reaching 449.06 GB/sec and write speeds at 188.51 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng tests and Geekbench multi-core scores are rated as strong, supported by high multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation performance. Database operations and PassMark memory scores also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench remains average, and LLM inference for large 70B models is poor during prompt processing, though it maintains average speeds during text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32pls_v6 offers a balanced profile for compute-intensive workloads that do not require high memory-to-core ratios. The dedicated ARM architecture provides high resource density and strong multi-threaded throughput without the overhead of hyper-threading. This makes the instance suitable for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, software compilation, and database operations. It is less suitable for memory-heavy databases or large-scale AI model inference due to its 2.0 GB per core memory limitation and lack of GPU acceleration.
